DarkLight · analysis update · 30 September 2026

Why the simulated spectrometer lines miss the data — and the fix

The simulation used the calculated dipole field scaled with current. The real magnets give 3–4 % more field per amp, and saturate. The simulation now takes each run's field from its own Hall probe. The beam energy is the remaining unknown, and it depends on the RF phases as well as on MB4.

measured / calculated field at equal current, TRIUMF map, last supply+3.3 %
share of the offset the field mapping explains (right arm, 150 A)92 %
run-to-run scatter after the fix (right arm, 8 runs)0.026 %
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 20261 / 48
Everything in this talk was redone with the new slow-control simulation pipeline on 29–30 Sep 2026: 80 elastic-line runs and 35 Møller runs. Numbers are relative to the Hall-probe constants installed on 30 Sep.

Summary

The answer in five points

  1. Cause. The simulation set the spectrometer field from the ANSYS calculation, scaled linearly with the dipole current. Measured at TRIUMF at the same current, the magnet gives 3.3 % more field (last, most trustworthy power supply), and its field per amp falls 0.5 % from 135 to 170 A (saturation). The quoted “1.063” was an artefact: 200 A data against a map normalised to 192 A.
  2. Size. The elastic lines need 4.2–4.6 % (right) and 4.6–5.5 % (left) more field than the calculation at 135–170 A. Mapping plus saturation predict 4.00 % of the 4.36 % needed on the right arm at 150 A: 92 %. At 200 A the beam extrapolates to 1.037 / 1.038 against TRIUMF's 1.033.
  3. Fix. Every simulated event now gets p₀ = K × |Bprobe| from the run's own Hall probe (g4DL /run/slowControl). K is fixed per arm and per probe position from the elastic lines. The right-arm scan is then flat to 0.026 %.
  4. Beam energy. Only the MB4 formula gives it. Between tunes it is off by 0.3–0.4 % (15, 28.7 MeV), and by 1.5–1.7 % in the two tunes near 20 MeV. Two runs at the same MB4 current, with different injector/buncher phase setpoints, differ by 1.4 %: the RF sets the energy too.
  5. Open. The absolute energy scale (0.3–0.5 % residual after the field), a left-arm offset/trend, the field at low currents (Møller settings), and line widths 3× the simulation.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 20262 / 48
If you remember one thing: the field was wrong by a known, measured amount, and the simulation now follows the Hall probes. What remains is dominated by how well we know the beam energy.

A · The problem

At the calculated field, the simulated elastic line lands 26 mm from the data

Run 4405, right arm (20°), 150 A, 24.48 MeV, bottom-GEM X. Left: the simulation with the calculated field (ANSYS map × I / 225 A) puts the line 26 mm away: the data need 4.38 % more field. Right: with p₀ = K × |Bprobe| the data sit between simulations at 0.99 and 1.01 (scale 1.0003).
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 20264 / 48
The dispersive coordinate moves about 6 mm per % of field at 24.5 MeV, so a 4 % field error is a 26 mm line shift.

A · The problem

How a line position becomes a field scale

  • Generator: elastic e–¹²C with radiative tail (darklight_scattering), at the run's beam energy.
  • Simulation: g4DL tracks through the ANSYS field map, scaled to the spectrometer momentum.
  • Digitisation and clustering: the same GEMini code and channel map as the data.
  • Fit: gaus + pol1 to the line on the bottom-GEM X axis, data and each simulation alike.
  • Interpolate: two simulations bracket the data (±1 %); the straight line through them has slope g = −5.94 ± 0.007 mm per %. The data line crosses it at scale 1.0003 ± 0.0000 (statistical, data and simulation).
  • A beam-energy error moves the line exactly like a field error: the line measures pelastic / p₀.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 20265 / 48
The measurement is differential: data and simulation go through identical clustering and fitting, so detector effects cancel. What is left is the ratio of the elastic momentum to the spectrometer central momentum.

Data and simulation on the detector plane

Bottom GEM of the right arm, events with one cluster per axis, log colour scale. The simulation (calculated field) has the line at the wrong X; the non-dispersive (Y) acceptance and the line shape agree. The data line is 3× wider (section G). The radiative tail of the generated spectrum spreads to lower momentum (smaller X) under the background.

B · Field calculation vs field mapping

What was measured, what the simulation uses

Calculation (used by g4DL)

  • ANSYS map B_field_20250109: the 60-turn magnet at 225 A = 35.157 MeV/c central momentum.
  • g4DL scales the whole map by p₀ / 35.157, i.e. linearly with current. No saturation, no hysteresis.
  • COMSOL maps exist but cover only ±19 mm vertically, and their current is not recorded.

Mapping (TRIUMF, early 2025)

  • 1D Hall probe, 5 mm grid over 340 × 350 mm at three heights (−3, 0, +3 mm): 14,697 points per map.
  • Two magnets, SN01 and SN02, at 200 A (technician). SN02 mapped on 30 Jan and 27 Feb with the first supply; spot-checked on 1 Apr with a second supply that reads 1.0–1.25 % higher.
  • Which magnet is on which arm is not known.

Independent re-fit (~/Field_Studies/review)

  • Measured points against the ANSYS map with free rotation, two in-plane offsets, height offset, scale, and probe tilt (the probe orientation is unknown).
  • Probe tilt fitted: 1.2–1.6° (SN02), 4.5° (SN01); it changes the scale by ≤ 0.3 %.
  • The original Mapping.C / Field_fitting.cpp reproduced, with small bugs (round() instead of floor() in the interpolation, degenerate offsets, an off-by-one); none moves the scale by more than 0.04 %.
  • Opposite handedness of the coordinate transform excluded (rms 468 G vs 9 G).
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 20267 / 48
Nobody knows which serial number is on which arm, and the power-supply calibration differs by 1 % between the two supplies used at TRIUMF. Both limit how well the mapping can predict the beam result.

B · Field calculation vs field mapping

The quoted 1.063 compared 200 A data with the map at 192 A

  • Mapping.C normalises the map by 0.85333 = (240 A × 48 turns)/(225 A × 60 turns): the 30 MeV/c = 192 A setting.
  • The measurements are at 200 A, so 4 % of the 6.3 % is the current mismatch: at equal current the ratio is 1.021–1.030.
  • The last power supply reads 1.0097–1.0125× the first at the same set current. With it, SN02 is 1.033–1.034.
  • So the magnet has 2–3.4 % more field per amp than calculated; the spread is the current calibration.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 20268 / 48
1.063 should not be used anywhere: it compares two different currents. The design constant 1/716.22 × 30/192 × 40 = 0.008726 MeV/c per G is the reference for K.

B · Field calculation vs field mapping

In the mapped region one scale factor describes the field

SN02 (27 Feb) against the fitted ANSYS map (scale, position, probe tilt). Left: ratio − 1 at mid-height, field above 5 % of peak. Right: mean and rms of the ratio in bins of field level. Above 90 % of the peak one scale factor fits to 0.14 % rms; at 30–70 % of the peak the measurement is 0.3–0.4 % higher, and below 30 % it falls 1–7 % faster than calculated. Integrated along lines through the magnet the scaled calculation agrees to 0.03 %: the fringe differences are worth 0.1–0.2 % of ∫B dl and are absorbed into K.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 20269 / 48
The important point: the shape of the calculated field is right; only its normalisation is off. That is why one number per arm (K) can fix it.

B · Field calculation vs field mapping

The magnets saturate; the scaled map does not

In-situ Hall-probe reading per amp for every stable-current run after the last probe move. Over the elastic-scan range (135–170 A) B/I falls ~0.5 %; the calculation scaled with current stays flat. Below ~100 A the value depends on how the current was reached (hysteresis): 0.05–0.2 % at 140–175 A, 0.3–0.9 % at 60–90 A, 1–3 % at 15–40 A. The two probes sit at different positions, so their absolute B/I differ by ~1 %.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202610 / 48
Hysteresis is why the probe must be read in every run: at a given current the field depends on the history by up to 0.9 % at 60-90 A.

The beam sees the same saturation as the Hall probe

Change with current, relative to 150 A; straight-line fits (errors from the fit residuals). Left arm: the line needs −0.240 ± 0.022 % per 10 A against −0.089 ± 0.008 % in the probe: an extra trend, open (section G).

B · Field calculation vs field mapping

The field mapping explains 92 % of the offset

  • Right arm at 150 A (run 4405). The factors multiply: 1.0335 (TRIUMF, last supply) × 1.0063 (saturation from 200 A to 150 A, from the probe's B/I slope, ± 0.05 %) = 1.0400. The lines need 1.0436: residual × 1.0034.
  • The left arm needs 5.1 % at 150 A but falls faster with current (−0.24 % per 10 A, against −0.09 % in its probe); extrapolated to 200 A it needs 1.038, like the right arm. The extra slope is the open left-arm trend (section G).
  • The residual 0.34 % (0.4–0.5 % at 200 A) is within: the 1 % current-calibration spread between supplies, an MB4 beam-energy error of the size seen between tunes, and the unknown SN01/SN02 assignment (SN01 +1 %).
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202613 / 48
What is left, a few tenths of a percent, is the size of the known calibration uncertainties. It cannot be split further without a current calibration or an independent beam energy.

C · The fix

Set the spectrometer momentum from the Hall probe

p₀ = Karm × |Bprobe|
  • Shape: keep the ANSYS map. One scale fits the measured field to ~0.1 % inside the magnet.
  • Scale: from the run's own Hall probe, event by event. This follows saturation, hysteresis and drifts automatically; a correction written as “constant × current” would be wrong by up to 0.5 % across the operating range.
  • K: fixed per arm from the elastic lines of the 24.48 MeV scans, i.e. with the MB4 beam energy. K is valid only for one probe position (next slides).
  • Fringe correction: not applied (0.1–0.2 %; absorbed into K).
  • The same K reconstructs momenta in data (simple_physics) and sets them in simulation.

K is fitted with the MB4 beam energy, so K absorbs any absolute beam-energy error at 24.5 MeV. Relative energies between tunes are unaffected.

C · The fix

Simulating a data run: the slow-control pipeline

  • Only simulations that read slow control take the data run number and the one-event GEM delay; all other simulations are unchanged (run 10201, no delay).
  • Nothing is set by hand: K from cutsDB.ini for the run, |B| from the run's probe at each mapped DAQ event (stored per event as SC_Left/RightProbe and SC_Left/RightMom).
  • /det/fieldScale is optional and defaults to 1. It is an extra factor on K × |B|, used only by fieldcal to make the ±1 % brackets (0.99 / 1.01); production macros leave it out.
  • Fixed on the way: a left-field sign flip in SetLMomentum; RadMoller's first-event crash.

C · The fix

Within a run the line follows the Hall probe

  • Run 4407, right arm, 160 A: the elastic line in time slices, the Hall probe, and the probe temperature.
  • The probe drifts 0.13 G over three minutes and the line moves with it, at the slope a field change implies.
  • So the probe measures the field the electrons see, also within a run. The simulation uses the probe reading of each event.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202619 / 48

C · The fix

The Hall probes move when a GEM is replaced

  • Dec 15 2025 (run 3252), left bottom GEM replaced: left probe −3.1 %.
  • Jan 23 2026 (runs 4077 → 4078), right top GEM swapped: left +1.7 %, right +0.9 %.
  • Scatter within a period is hysteresis (current history); a move is a step at every current across a GEM intervention.
  • Found from the GEM failure/repair list and every slow-control file since run 1017.

D · Beam energy

The beam energy only comes from the MB4 formula

Beam momentum relative to the accelerator's formula E = 0.235 × IMB4 + 0.013 MeV, normalised to the 24.48 MeV tune (joint fits: one field model and one X offset per arm, one momentum factor per tune; 19.9 MeV from the ratio to the 20.0 MeV runs at the same current). Both arms agree wherever both measured. The 19.9 MeV tune and the 20.0 MeV runs 4091–4097 sit at −1.5 to −1.7 %; run 4090, with 4091's MB4 current but different RF phase setpoints, sits at −0.4 % with the other tunes.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202622 / 48
Everything here is relative, because K was fixed with the MB4 energy at 24.48 MeV. An absolute beam-energy error at 24.48 MeV would show up as a K error.

D · Beam energy

MB4 alone cannot give the energy

  • At MB4 ≈ 85 A the beam momentum takes three different values relative to the formula: −0.4 % (run 4090), −1.5 % (the 19.9 MeV tune, 84.67 A) and −1.7 % (runs 4091–4097). Only the RF settings differ.
  • MB4 hysteresis (the 24.5 MeV tune was reached from above, all others from below) and MB4 saturation were fitted to the offsets: both fail badly (χ² ≫ ndf).
  • The offsets are tune-specific: the energy depends on the RF amplitudes and phases, which MB4 does not track.
  • So the MB4 energy of any tune is uncertain by ≳ 0.4 %, and by ≳ 1.5 % if the RF phase setpoints were changed.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202624 / 48
The MB4 formula is the accelerator group's calibration; it assumes the energy is set by the bend. The data say the RF matters at the percent level.

D · Beam energy

MB4 hysteresis, saturation or a wrong formula offset cannot explain the offsets

  • Each model gives a tune's offset e (relative to 24.5 MeV) from its MB4 current alone, with one free parameter.
  • Hysteresis (MB4 not cycled): the field on the branch reached from above is higher by h amps. e = −h/2 (1/I + 1/I24.5) from below; +h/2 (1/I − 1/I24.5) from above (24.5, 19.9 MeV).
  • Saturation: e = −β (I² − I24.5²). Formula offset: E = formula + δE.
  • Errors: stat ⊕ 0.1 % per tune ⊕ 0.2 % at 15 MeV (probe transfer).

D · Beam energy

Within one tune the energy can be stable or wander

  • 24.48 MeV set (17 runs, 15M events): rms 0.012 % = 3 keV. Its mean scale, 1.00135, equals scan run 4414 at the same current (1.00134): K and the beam were stable across these days. On the right arm, runs 4349/4357 (the Møller-test days) agree with scan run 4405 at 150 A to 0.03 %.
  • 28.71 MeV set (29 runs): rms 0.08 % = 23 keV, with a +0.3 % step after the empty runs 4231–4232 that relaxes over ~5 h. No recorded setpoint, RF readback, BPM or current follows it; only environment and beam-loss proxies correlate.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202628 / 48

D · Beam energy

What the slow control can and cannot tell us

  • 28.71 MeV set in 2-minute slices: the elastic line after the Hall-probe correction, and PVs that vary. Grey band: the empty runs 4231–4232.
  • BPMs are frozen: every run of a set carries the same value, time-stamped 1–13 h before the run (tune-up). BPM5/6A/6B read 0.
  • RF: only the amplitudes are measured; they vary by 1–2 × 10⁻⁴ and do not follow the line. No phase is measured.
  • No setpoint changed between consecutive runs; only environment and beam-loss proxies (temperatures, vacuum gauges, the gun BPM, the beam current) correlate with the line.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202629 / 48

D · Beam energy

Two energies at one current: a GEM X offset cannot reconcile them

  • Runs 4418 (24.48 MeV) and 4219 (28.71 MeV): left dipole at 165.05 A in both, so the same field (probes differ by 0.08 %, taken out). Correct MB4 energies would give both the same p₀ / (K × |B|).
  • At zero offset they differ by 0.66 %. A GEM X offset shifts both lines by the same mm, but the lines sit at different places on the plane, so their implied scales move differently; they agree only at dx = +22 mm.
  • Excluded: the top GEM (same line, different distance) gives an offset common to both planes of −0.2 ± 2.8 mm (run 4412); the joint fit of all energies gives +6.7 ± 0.9 mm.
  • So the MB4 energies are not consistent: relative to 24.5 MeV the 28.7 MeV beam is 0.46 % lower than MB4 says at the joint-fit offset (the joint fit itself: −0.42 ± 0.05 %), 0.66 % at the top-GEM value.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202630 / 48

E · Møller scattering

The Møller band: a simultaneous beam monitor

Right arm at 37.1 A during the 28.71 MeV set sits on single-arm Møller scattering at 20°; the left arm measured the elastic line at the same time. The band X(Y) is tilted because Y follows the horizontal scattering angle; its position is fitted as u = X − 1.8 Y (truncated mean). Simulation: RadMoller at the run's energy, g4DL in slow-control mode.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202631 / 48

E · Møller scattering

How the Møller band position is measured

  • Events with exactly one cluster on each axis of the right bottom GEM, Y between −30 and +30 mm (a hot strip at Y 14–20 mm removed).
  • Along the band X grows with Y (Y follows the horizontal scattering angle). u = X − 1.8 Y projects the band onto one peak; the slope 1.8 is fixed from the band's ridge: the peak of u in 10 mm slices of Y is flat to ~2 mm (u = 4.5, 3.6, 4.2, 5.3, 5.5, 5.4 mm at Y = −25, −15, …, +25 mm).
  • Position = iterated truncated mean of u within ±20 mm of itself (shaded): robust against the broad background and tails. A gaus + pol1 fit over ±30 mm is the cross-check.
  • Data and simulation are treated identically; statistical errors 0.05–0.07 mm per run.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202632 / 48

E · Møller scattering

Møller and elastic respond differently to beam energy, position and angle

  • From simulation, not data: RadMoller (Møller) and darklight_scattering (elastic) through g4DL, changing one thing at a time — beam energy +1 %, beam spot +2 mm in x or y, beam direction +2 mrad about y or x — and fitting the band and the line exactly as in data; values per 1 % / 1 mm / 1 mrad of the actual change.
  • As an energy calibration the band is weak: 1.2 mm per % (elastic 6.3), and 1 mrad of beam angle equals 2 % of energy.
  • As a monitor it separates the causes: the ratio of Møller to elastic shifts is +0.20 for energy, +1.05 for vertical beam position, and ≫ 1 for horizontal position or angle.

E · Møller scattering

The elastic-line wander in the 28.7 MeV set is beam energy

Both lines as data − slow-control simulation, per run. The fitted slope, −0.10 ± 0.18, agrees with a pure energy change (+0.20, 1.6σ) and excludes vertical beam motion (+1.05, 6σ). The Møller band has its own run-to-run scatter (0.48 mm against 0.10 mm statistical) and drifts +0.6 mm through the set: beam direction changes, visible only in the Møller band.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202634 / 48
The Møller band is five times less sensitive to energy than the elastic line but equally sensitive to vertical beam position, which makes the ratio a clean discriminator.

E · Møller scattering

At 34–38 A the band needs 1.1–1.5 % less field — not a constant offset

  • Left plot — right spectrometer (runs 4159/4163/4166, 38.1/36.1/34.1 A, 19.91 MeV): data − simulation +6.8/+6.5/+6.2 mm; the 28.7 MeV set at 37.1 A: +8.2 mm. The band moves 5.6 mm per % of field (60 mm across the three runs), so 1.1–1.5 %, or a 2.5–3 mrad horizontal beam angle.
  • A constant field offset in gauss would grow as 1/B; the data shrink. Ruled out (χ² 60/2); a constant (χ² 13/2) is better but not good. Fit parameters in the legends.
  • Right plot — left spectrometer (runs 4349/4379/4357, 12–17 A, 2–3 MeV/c): −33/−18/−10 mm, steeply field-dependent; no model fits.
  • At 12–17 A the probe-scaled map is not a good description (remanence, field shape); the K from 135–170 A does not transfer.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202635 / 48
A field deficit that grows at low excitation, or a beam-angle offset. The right-arm test cannot separate these two; a low-field map could.

E · Møller scattering

Low-momentum settings need the other dipole's stray field

Left arm, run 4349 (12 A, 2.0 MeV/c Møller electrons at 36°). The old simulation had the right dipole off; the slow-control simulation sets it from its probe (150 A in this run). The stray field moves the band by 2.9 mm (12 A) and 1.6 mm (17 A); in run 4379, with the right dipole at 14.7 A, nothing moves. Any simulation of low-momentum settings must include both dipoles — the slow-control mode does this automatically.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202636 / 48

E · Møller scattering

How far the dipole fields reach in the simulation

  • g4DL uses one ANSYS map for both dipoles: a box 1 m × 1 m (transverse) × 1.5 m (along the arm) that starts at the target, rotated to each arm. Inside the box it is the calculated field of the whole magnet, fringe included; outside it is zero.
  • The arms are 56° apart, so each dipole's box covers the first 0.6 m of the other arm's path. At 150 A the right dipole gives 0.2 G at the target and 2.4–3.3 G at 0.3–0.6 m — more than the left dipole's own fringe at 12 A for the first ~0.35 m.
  • Not validated: TRIUMF mapped only above 5 % of the peak near the magnet centre. Beyond the box the field is cut to zero.
  • Not in g4DL: the Earth's field (~0.5 G, the same size; it bends a 2 MeV/c electron by ~7 mrad over 1 m), and the upstream beamline magnets (MB2, MB4, the quadrupoles and steerers), which act on the beam before the target. The downstream quadrupoles are in g4DL but off by default and act only inside their 2.6–3.3 cm apertures.

F · Inelastic ¹²C lines

The inelastic lines cannot give an absolute energy scale

The 4.44 MeV state sits a fixed Eₓ below the elastic line, so it would fix the momentum scale independently of the field. Shaded: fit window. Scan (bottom): open points have a fit window reaching the block of empty strips at X ≈ −164 to −154 mm (24.48 MeV set: Eₓ ≥ 4.7 MeV; fits at 5.0–5.1 MeV fail there). Method on the next slide.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202638 / 48

F · Inelastic ¹²C lines

The statistical analysis of the search

  • Prediction: Npred = Nelastic × σ(4.44)/σel × acceptance ratio. σ from the form factor |FC2|² = (4π/Z²)(q²/15)² B(E2↑) with B(E2↑) = 39.7 e²fm⁴ (q ≈ 0.075 fm⁻¹): 1.6 × 10⁻⁶. The acceptance ratio and the line position and width come from the elastic simulation at the rescaled field (rigidity scaling, checked with a direct simulation to 0.02 mm).
  • Spectra: all bottom-GEM clusters (h_all), a Y window (h_ywin), and a matching top-GEM cluster in X, Y or both (h_cx, h_cy, h_cxy).
  • Fit: a Gaussian of fixed position and width with free amplitude A (may be negative) on a pol3 background over ±40 mm; χ² with Poisson likelihood where bins are small. Single-strip artifacts (> 5σ + 5 % off their ±5-bin median) are masked.
  • Error: strip structure dominates, so the same fit is repeated at ~90 line-free positions across the plane; the spread (1.4826 × MAD) is σemp, used when larger than σstat.
  • Limit: 90 % CL with a flat prior on A ≥ 0 and a Gaussian likelihood of width max(σstat, σemp); the largest over background orders 2–4 and windows ±30/40/50 mm is quoted. An injected signal of 5 × UL is recovered exactly.
  • Combination: signal strength μ = A / Npred per set, weighted mean, same limit rule: μ < 2.35 × 10³ → B(E2↑) < 9.3 × 10⁴ e²fm⁴ (literature 39.7); Hoyle state M(E0) < 1.3 × 10³ fm² (5.47).

G · GEM and beam offsets

GEM positions: channel map fixed, no offset on the right, +6.7 mm on the left

  • Channel map: GEMini converts strip n to X = 0.4 mm × n − 200.4 mm (half of the 1002 connected strips). Every GEM has 11 X and 6 Y unconnected channels at each end; before the fix n counted from the first APV channel, 11 channels early. So the fix moves every plane of both arms by −4.4 mm in X and −2.4 mm in Y. Measured on the right scan: −4.4 to −4.6 mm (4407: −3.6, its line sat on mis-assigned dead strips). The left scans were first analysed after the fix, so no before/after exists for them.
  • Right arm: no X offset needed (−1.1 ± 0.7 mm).
  • Left arm (after the fix, unrelated to it): the joint fit over all energies wants +6.7 ± 0.9 mm, or equivalently the −0.3 % scale trend. The top GEM (usable only in run 4412) sees the same line: offset common to both planes −0.2 ± 2.8 mm, so not a bottom-GEM offset.
  • Bottom GEMs are the same chambers for all runs ≥ 3252; LG0 was a different chamber before.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202640 / 48

G · GEM and beam offsets

Beam position and width at the target are not measured

  • Vertical beam position at the target moves the elastic line +0.80 mm per mm (0.13 % in momentum per mm); horizontal −0.06 mm/mm. A 5 mm vertical difference between tunes would look like a 0.6 % energy change.
  • g4DL has a commented-out target survey offset, y = −4.877 mm. If real but not simulated, the elastic lines shift ~3.9 mm and the fitted K absorbs it (≈ 0.6 %), because for the elastic line a height offset and a field error look alike. But it is not a field error: the Møller band responds with a different ratio (0.85 mm per mm vs 1.2 mm per % of energy), so K would then be wrong for other kinematics. It belongs in the geometry once confirmed, and K refitted.
  • Line width: data 3× the simulation at every energy (2.6–3.6 mm vs 1.2–1.3 mm). Needs a vertical beam size σy ≈ 3–4 mm or an energy spread of 0.4–0.55 %, different between tunes. Not understood.
  • The Møller band excludes vertical beam motion as the cause of the 28.7 MeV wander (section E).

H · Status

What every other analysis has to do

Data

  • Central momentum from the Hall probe: p₀ = K × |Bprobe|, K from cutsDB.ini for the run. Never from the current.
  • When a GEM is replaced the probe moves: add a [run:N] section and transfer or refit K.
  • Treat the MB4 beam energy as uncertain: ~0.4 % between tunes, more if the RF was re-phased. Measure each tune's relative energy with an elastic line where possible.

Simulation of a data run

  • g4DL: /run/slowControl run<N>_slowcontrol.root before /run/initialize; do not set the spectrometer momenta by hand.
  • Generators: slowcontrol = <file> (darklight_scattering), -S <file> (RadMoller).
  • Digitise and cluster as usual: the run number selects the GEM configuration and the one-event delay.
  • Simulations that are not of a data run are unchanged.

H · Status

Open problems, in order of impact

highAbsolute beam energy. K carries the MB4 energy at 24.48 MeV. The field budget leaves 0.3–0.5 % that could be beam energy or current calibration; tunes differ by 0.3–1.7 % from MB4, set partly by the RF.
highLow-field settings. Møller at 34–38 A needs 1.1–1.5 % less field (or a 2.5–3 mrad beam angle); at 12–17 A the probe-scaled map fails. K from 135–170 A cannot be used there.
mediumLeft arm. A −0.3 % scale trend over 135–170 A not seen by its probe, equivalent to a +6.7 mm X offset that the top GEM does not support.
mediumLine width. Data 3× the simulation: beam size or energy spread, not modelled.
mediumCurrent calibration and magnet identity. TRIUMF supplies differ by 1.0–1.25 %; SN01/SN02 ↔ arm unknown.
lowEarlier probe positions. K transferred by B/I, good to 0.2–0.3 %; no elastic runs to check before run 3252.
lowBeam position at the target not recorded (BPMs frozen); target survey value y = −4.877 mm unconfirmed.

The first two items limit every analysis that needs absolute momenta; the others are percent-level for special settings or sub-percent.

H · Status

Measurements that would settle the open problems

  1. Dipole current readbacks against a DCCT or calibrated shunt. Separates the current calibration from the field and from the beam energy.
  2. A Hall-probe reading with each dipole at 200 A (no beam needed), and the SN01/SN02 assignment. Compares directly with TRIUMF and removes the extrapolation from 170 A.
  3. An independent beam-energy measurement for at least one tune (accelerator-side, or a dedicated DarkLight method), and recorded RF phase and drive readbacks for every run.
  4. Continuous BPM readings and a target survey (target height, spectrometer angles).
  5. The field at low excitation (≤ 40 A): a map or remanence measurement, for Møller and other low-momentum settings.
Spectrometer field and beam energy · DarkLight · 30 September 202645 / 48

H · Status

Summary

  • The data/simulation offset is mainly the field: the magnets give 3.3 % more field per amp than calculated (TRIUMF, last supply) and saturate by 0.5 % over the scan range. Together they account for 92 % of the offset on the right arm.
  • The simulation now takes the field from each run's Hall probe, event by event, with one K per arm and probe position. The right scan is flat to 0.03 %; the 24.5 MeV sets agree across days to 10⁻⁵.
  • The remaining unknown is the beam energy: the MB4 formula is off by 0.3–1.7 % between tunes, and changing only the RF phase setpoints moved it 1.4 %.
  • Møller scattering confirms the elastic wander is energy, not beam position, and shows the low-field field is not yet described.
  • The inelastic lines are too weak for an absolute energy; GEM offsets are fixed (channel map) or excluded, except the left-arm trend.

Appendix

Terms, tools and where things are

Terms

  • scale: field (or p₀) the data imply ÷ the reference p₀ of the simulation.
  • calculated field: ANSYS map × I / 225 A (the old reference).
  • probe anchor: K × |Bprobe| over the clustered data events (the new reference).
  • K: MeV/c of central momentum per G of Hall-probe reading, per arm and probe position.
  • e: beam momentum ÷ MB4 formula − 1, relative to the 24.48 MeV tune.

Where

  • Results: fieldcal/sc/ (REPORT.txt, summary.csv, run<N>/result.json), fieldcal/analysis/multi_energy_sc.txt, scstudy/moller/sc/report.txt, inelastic_combined/report.txt, scstudy/SUMMARY.md.
  • Field review: ~/Field_Studies/review/ (fieldfit.C, comsolfit.C, fit_results.txt).
  • Tools: tools/fieldcal/ (fieldcal.py, specmom.py), tools/scstudy/probe_epochs.py, tools/inelastic/.
  • This deck: fieldcal/talk_field/ (data.py → figs.py → build.py).
